scenes.vo: One student's squat, on any body.
Between physio visits, you do your home exercises alone. Your physio can't watch every rep.
So your physio records the exercise once. Simon turns it into a 3D reference.
At home, you follow it side by side, and live check marks the joints that drift.
Then SAM 3.1, SAM 3D Body and Muse Spark analyse the take.
The result: C, 72 percent of the points. The first note comes at its moment: straighten your arms. Turn the 3D view to see where the two bodies differ.
Fix it for me replays that moment on your own body, with the arms moved to the recorded pose. Muse Spark watches both videos and agrees with all four notes.
Every result lists the Meta models behind it, and whether each one ran live.
One picture of a character becomes a rigged model. SAM 3D Objects builds the shape, SAM 3D Body and the MHR body give it a skeleton, and it performs your take.
Any body plays the same take on several bodies at once.
You stay in control. You agree before each take, can keep only the 3D model and drop the video, and can delete any take from its result.
One take costs Simon about 7 cents in API calls. An hour with a personal trainer costs 40 to 75 dollars.
Simon. Learn any movement from one recording.
